needsYou.title: Turn on GitHub's own leak-blocker for the Drape repository (one click, your account)
needsYou.productImpact: Tonight's check catches a leaked key when a change is proposed. GitHub can also refuse the upload itself, seconds earlier, before the key is anywhere anyone else can see it. That switch is off on the repository — the block we hit tonight came from a setting on the uploading account, which a different account would not have.
needsYou.workedExample: When I deliberately uploaded a fake OpenRouter key to test the new check, GitHub refused the upload outright ("push declined … OpenRouter API Key"). That refusal was luck of the account, not a property of the repo: GitHub → Drape repository → Settings → Code security → "Push protection" is OFF. Turning it on makes that refusal apply to every account and every branch.
needsYou.recommendation: Turn it on. Repository settings are yours, not the team's; it is free and has no effect on customers.

eyeItems.question: Does the creative register (arm C) reach your raw prompt’s conviction (arm A, and your two reference frames) while keeping sheet structure? Check each frame against your own list: jaw plate present and prominent, amber eye glowing, porcelain committed, no beards you never asked for, build spread not converged, wardrobe line obeyed. Refusal counts are under each strip’s caption.

frames.caption: Your reference frame 1 — the conviction bar, made by your own raw prompt.
Your reference frame 2 — the second raw-prompt frame.
Your raw prompt + your seven words of frame, re-made tonight. 0 of 3 refused. This is the bar the candidate must reach.
Today’s full compile, through the real entrance. 0 of 3 refused — but look: beards you never asked for on all three, t-shirts against the bare-chested ask, and the hardware gone timid.

THE CANDIDATE — the creative register: your words verbatim, a minimal frame, a per-slice variance card. 1 of 3 refused. Hardware committed — but the mid-torso framing line was ignored (full body delivered), so the lean frame loses locks the old scaffolding held.
The candidate minus the variance card. 2 OF 3 REFUSED — the card appears to protect against refusals as well as buying spread.
The candidate plus the one-sentence category block. 2 of 3 refused.

RERUN, now valid: the same three compiles as B with every house block cut to its first clause and YOUR facts kept word for word (12,500 → 3,300 characters). 0 of 3 refused. Against B: the beards, the shirts and the missing porcelain are still here — shortening did not fix them, so those answers are WRONG, not long. What it bought is conviction: a solid jaw plate in frames 1 and 3, and a tighter mid-torso frame.
The writer’s room: “cyber-goth girl with an eyepatch”, authored into rich concepts, rendered. 1 of 3 refused; the author gave 4 concepts of the 8 asked.
The same thin brief through today’s compile — the control for the writer’s room.

pipeline.title: A second automatic security reader now scans every proposed change for known-dangerous code shapes (#33)
pipeline.note: in this deploy; team tooling, nothing a customer sees. It looks for the classic mistakes — building database queries from text, running user text as code, writing user text straight into a page. I did not trust it until it had been caught out: I planted two dangerous lines and it found both; the same plant in a throw-away script folder was correctly ignored. It also MISSED one planted shape (running a shell command from a web request), which is written on its record page rather than hidden. Its first read of the product: four notes, all one harmless pattern in the homepage image route — and opening that file to annotate them found a small real bug: asking for a hero image called 'constructor' got a server error instead of a plain 'not found'. Fixed, with a test that fails on the old code.

pipeline.title: The team's dead-code detector is in — one command lists every file, export and dependency nothing uses (#34)
pipeline.note: in this deploy. It is a READER, never a deleter: the Atlas keeps the only authority to remove anything. Proven both ways before it counted — a planted dead file and a planted dead export were both caught, and the five modules our older map once wrongly called unused (both login routes among them) are correctly left alone. First reading: 51 unused files (40 of them unused UI primitives from the component kit), 34 unused packages, 174 unused exports. Nothing was deleted; the Janitor's first patrol takes it from here.

journal.text: Still no word from you on the court strips, so the creative register stays parked at its gate and this was maintenance again. Its first read of the product came back with four notes, all one harmless pattern in the homepage image route — and opening that file to explain them turned up a small real bug: asking for a hero image named 'constructor' produced a server error instead of a plain 'not found'. Fixed, with a test that fails on the old code, and checked that the two similar routes were already safe. Another seat's workflow-checker change (#35) went green at 06:17 and is still waiting to be merged; if it is still sitting there the next shift merges it. One of the automatic dependency updates is failing for a real reason (a type change in the image library), noted for the next shift. Nothing was spent. Still waiting on you: the eight court strips, the GitHub one-click, and the OpenRouter balance.

The reviewer found real gaps across five rounds — one shape of the OpenRouter key would have slipped through, and a secret sharing a line with a cast id would have been hidden — and each was closed and re-proven. One thing for you: GitHub has its own upload-time blocker and it is switched off for the repository (card above, one click).
